messages:
raj: quick heads-up — found a nasty difference between py/ts SDK payloads for POST /v1/generate. py client serializes stop=[] as null, ts client sends an empty array. server treats null as omit but [] as explicit empty -> different behavior.

sasha: ugh. that explains the flaky test we saw in canary. which behavior does the REST contract expect?

claire: the intent in the API contract was: omitted stop => server default, null is considered missing, empty array => explicit no-stops (allowed). but runtime historically normalized null -> omit. seems the python serialization changed recently. do we have a spec page entry?

raj: there isn't a clear line in the openapi that says null vs []. the schema has "stop": {"oneOf": [{"type":"string"}, {"type":"array", "items":{"type":"string"}}], "nullable": true} which is ambiguous for clients.

michael: we should pick one canonical behavior. my vote: clients should omit the field when they mean default; sending [] should be explicit. server should accept null as omit for backward compat, but want clients consistent.

raj: here's what I saw in the py SDK (v1.4.2) behavior:
```python
# user call
client.generate(model="lucid-7b", prompt="hi", stop=[])
# serialized payload (what gets sent)
{"model":"lucid-7b","prompt":"hi","stop":null}
```

sasha: and the TS SDK?

raj: ts (v2.0.1) does:
```ts
await client.generate({model: 'lucid-7b', prompt: 'hi', stop: []})
// payload
{"model":"lucid-7b","prompt":"hi","stop":[]}
```

claire: that mismatch will break consumers who rely on server semantics. it can lead to regressions: ts consumers get explicit no-stops, py consumers get server default.

michael: the runtime team prefers making server tolerant rather than forcing all clients to change immediately. we can treat null === omit. but long-term we should fix the SDKs to be explicit and match the openapi.

dev-bot: CI report: canary/generation-tests flaked 2x in last 24h — likely related to stop normalization. See #CI-1223 for logs.

raj: proposal: 1) patch python SDK to serialize empty list as [] not null (minor breaking? but expected), 2) add integration test that asserts server receives the raw JSON (no runtime-normalization surprises), 3) add explicit note in the openapi and docs about stop null vs omit vs [].

sasha: agree on tests and docs. for the py change — is it just the JSON encoder that treats empty list weirdly? I can look.

raj: I tracked it: the SDK uses pydantic model with allow_none and a custom dict(exclude_none=True) call. when stop is set to [] it's being coerced earlier into None by our param-normalizer if length==0 (we wanted to treat empty strings as None). bug.

claire: nice catch. that's an SDK bug, we should patch. low risk to change to keep [] when user passed a list.

michael: runtime will keep null==omit for now, but we should emit a warning in logs when we receive null for stop to help debug. also, can we add a backwards-compat header? maybe unnecessary.

raj: action items: @sasha to open py SDK PR to stop coercion (link please), @michael to add runtime log warning and check CI flakiness, @claire to update openapi and docs. I'll add unit + integration tests for both SDKs.

sasha: will open PR today — draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/412 (WIP). change is tiny: remove the empty-list coercion and ensure exclude_none preserves []. tests incoming. :thumbsup:

michael: I'll add a one-line server log and add a canary assertion to detect null-stop in request bodies. PR  https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2215.

claire: I'll update the OpenAPI: add "clarify-stop-null-omit-empty" note and an example matrix. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/98.

raj: quick checklist for the SDK PR: - unit test for serialize(stop=[]) -> payload contains [] - e2e test hitting local runtime to ensure behavior stable - changelog entry calling out bugfix.

sasha: working on tests now. ping me if you need a quick review, @claire @raj.

raj: thanks. reopening thread if anything changes. for record: reproducible curl that shows server sees null if py client unchanged:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"lucid-7b","prompt":"hi","stop":null}'
```

michael: noted. I'll watch CI after PRs land. :eyes:

claire: thanks team. once PRs are merged we'll roll a minor SDK release and add a short note in the release notes about the behavior.

sasha: done — opened PR #412 with tests. marking as draft until runtime logs are in.

dev-bot: Link to CI run with failing traces: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/1223 (flaky tests highlighted)
